response.evidence: The dataset has about 20 applications from Black or African American male applicants, and all of them were originated (0% denial). The overall denial rate across all groups is roughly 8-10%. Across all Black or African American applicants (about 50 records, including female and joint), there are about 5 denials, a rate similar to the overall rate. Most of those denials involve high debt-to-income ratios (50%-60%) or high loan-to-value ratios (95-100%), the same factors that appear in denials for other races. Confidence is limited because the Black male sample is small, the data lack variables such as credit score, and this simple comparison cannot rule out discrimination. It only shows no outcome disparity in this data.
